free_tier.stated: no account-level byte quota stated; per-file only — 10 MB images/GIFs, 25 MB other files, 10 MB video on free plan (100 MB on paid)

egress.terms: free and unmetered — 'For public repositories, uploaded files can be accessed without authentication'; served from githubusercontent CDN, cached by Camo

tooling: GitHub CLI: 'You can also attach local images and videos from the command line with GitHub CLI' (gh issue comment / gh pr comment --attach, changelog 2026-09-01); plus any REST client against the comment API
chaining: unlimited comments per issue x unlimited issues x unlimited free repos; 25 MB per non-image attachment. 1 GiB of payload = ~41 comments. Effectively per-record-unlimited storage keyed to comment IDs, not to an account quota
limits_note: 25 MB/file (10 MB images), per-comment attachment count not documented; uploads are immediate on attach, so a failed comment still leaves the asset

reliability_note: assets persist after comment edit/delete in practice (URL is anonymised and not reference-counted); bulk comment-creation is the one thing GitHub's usage-anomaly systems actually watch, and secondary rate limits are aggressive
